properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Northern Coastal Humboldt; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 12 at 3:02AM PDT until October 12 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...A very long period westerly swell will increase the
threat of sneaker waves.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Northern Coastal Humboldt,
Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...Through this evening. The risk will increase as winds
weaken.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
properties.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

NWSheadline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT NOW IN EFFECT THROUGH THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Yuma County; Kit Carson County; Cheyenne; Dundy
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 3:57AM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA... Yuma, Kit Carson, Cheyenne KS and Dundy
counties.

* TIMING... 9 AM MDT to 4 PM MDT (10 AM MDT to 5 PM CDT). Duration
of strong winds and low humidities together expected to be 1 to
2 hours.

* WINDS... West southwesterly 15 to 30 mph in the morning,
decreasing through the afternoon.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY... Falling to 10 to 15 percent in the
afternoon.

* TEMPERATURES... Lower to mid 80s.

* FUELS... Fuels will promote fire spread if fires were to
develop.

* FIRE DANGER...Lowest humidities will overlap with stronger
winds for an hour or two this afternoon. While not expected to
be widespread or persistent, these conditions could make
controlling any fire difficult.

Outdoor burning and activities that cause open sparks or flames
are discouraged. Fire and emergency officials should be aware that
weather conditions will be favorable for the development of grass
and crop fires.

NWSheadline: SPECIAL FIRE WEATHER STATEMENT

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 12 at 1:36AM PDT until October 12 at 8:00AM PDT by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.

* WHERE...Indian Wells Valley, Mojave Desert, and Mojave Desert
Slopes.

* WHEN...Until 8 AM PDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highways impacted include US Highway 395, and
State Routes 14, 58, and 178.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

NWSheadline: WIND ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 AM PDT THIS MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Eastern Cherry; Keya Paha; Boyd; Brown; Rock; Holt; Grant; Hooker; Thomas; Blaine; Loup; Western Cherry
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 12 at 3:32AM CDT by NWS North Platte NE
properties.description:
Patchy dense fog will continue across northern Nebraska and into
the Sandhills through sunrise. Some locations may see visibility
drop to near 1/4 mile briefly. Be prepeared for rapidly changing
conditions and allow for extra driving time this morning. Fog will
begin to dissipate by mid-morning after the sun rises.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 12 at 1:16AM PDT until October 13 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding due to morning high tides 6.5 to
7 feet in combination with surf 3-6 feet.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads during morning
high tides with only isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest high tides will occur between 10 AM
and 11 AM today and Tuesday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 2 PM PDT TUESDAY

properties.areaDesc: Waters from Cape Blanco OR to Pt. St. George CA from 10 to 60 nm
properties.headline: Hazardous Seas Warning issued October 12 at 1:08AM PDT until October 12 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...North winds 20 to 30 kt with a few gusts up to 40 kt
and steep to very steep wind-driven seas of 8 to 12 ft. Winds
ease to 10 to 20 kt and seas gradually subside to 6 to 8 ft
Monday night and Tuesday, but seas remain hazardous to small
craft.

* WHERE...All areas, with the strongest winds and steepest seas
from around Port Orford southward.

* WHEN...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, until 11 PM PDT this
evening. For the Small Craft Advisory, from 11 PM this evening
to 11 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong, gusty winds and steep to very steep
hazardous seas could capsize or damage vessels.

* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks
properties.instruction:
Recreational boaters should remain in port. Commercial vessels
should prepare for very steep seas and consider remaining in port
until conditions improve.
